gist: Patrick Ceresna's weekly MacroVoices trading desk covers four main points. The 10-year Treasury yield has broken above 5% (about 5.10%, highest since 2007) even as crude fell about $10, and Fed funds futures price ~70% odds of an October hike. The S&P 500 chart looks bullish while its breadth is collapsing, and DXY has broken out of an 18-month range above 101. The trade idea is a USO Jan-2027 $150/$180 bull call spread for renewed oil strength. Also covered: gold's possible false breakout, crowded but resilient copper, weak uranium equities, and a record flip to net-long yen positioning.

insights.claim: Trade idea for renewed crude strength with a defined premium: buy the USO January 15, 2027 $150 call for about $15.50 and sell the $180 call for about $7.25. That is an $8.25 net debit on a $30-wide spread (about 3:1 reward-to-risk), with USO referenced at $148.30 and about 113 days to expiry.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: An actionable options structure: maximum loss is the $8.25 debit if USO is at or below $150 at expiry, and the payoff is capped at USO $180, which Ceresna equates to roughly $120/bbl crude.
insights.quote: The structure is a bull call spread between the $150 to $180 strikes.

insights.claim: The oil volatility index has fallen toward the low end of its recent range and is well below this year's panic levels. That makes defined-risk long-oil options cheaper even though geopolitical supply risk to pipelines and export routes (per Michael Every) has not gone away.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: Low implied volatility against unresolved supply risk favors buying oil upside through options rather than outright futures.

insights.claim: The 10-year Treasury yield has decisively broken above 5% to about 5.10%, the highest since 2007. The 30-year is above 5.40% and the 10-year real yield is about 2.7%, and all this happened while crude oil fell nearly $10 from its highs, so oil is not what's driving bonds.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: Yields rising without an oil catalyst point to rate or funding pressure. Ceresna calls this the single most important driver of pricing across asset classes.

insights.claim: Fed funds futures price close to a 70% chance of a Fed rate hike in October, and more than a 50% chance of back-to-back hikes at both the October and December meetings.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: Markets now price a hiking cycle into year-end, a hawkish repricing that raises the hurdle rate for equities and hits duration-sensitive assets.

insights.claim: Patrick Ceresna says the speed of the yield rise matters more than its level. Yields rising this fast are usually when authorities try to calm bond markets, and whether they stabilize or fall another leg is the key thing to watch across assets.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: Watch for official intervention to stabilize long-end yields as a possible turning point for risk assets, gold and the dollar.

insights.claim: On price alone the S&P 500 is in a textbook bull trend: a bull flag that held the 50-day moving average and a breakout retesting prior highs. A move to 52-week highs could carry it to 8,000-8,200.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: Upside target of 8,000-8,200 if the index breaks to new highs and breadth widens.

insights.claim: Beneath the S&P 500 breakout, breadth is collapsing. The equal-weight S&P never rallied and is making lower lows, the Russell 2000 is on sell signals, financials are breaking to lower lows, and only 28% of stocks sit above their 50-day moving average, leaving about five mega-cap stocks to carry the index.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: Mega-cap concentration hides a fragile market. Equal-weight, small-cap and financials weakness is the tell to watch for a wider breakdown.
insights.quote: the number of stocks above their 50-day moving average is sitting at 28%

insights.claim: Patrick Ceresna's bias depends on yields. If the 10-year Treasury heads toward 5.25%-5.50%, that could break the bulls' hold and trigger a roughly 10% equity correction into the midterms, with mega-caps eventually joining the selling.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: 10-year at 5.25-5.50% is the trigger level for de-risking equities. A relief drop in yields would instead let breadth widen and support the bull case.

insights.claim: The 30-day VIX sits around 15, and the three-month VIX, which covers the elections, the next jobs data and the October earnings season, is at its lows for the year. That makes portfolio downside protection about as cheap as it has been all year.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: Stay long but buy cheap index puts or collars through year-end while implied volatility ignores the yield and breadth risks.
insights.quote: the cost of insuring is about as cheap as it's been all year

insights.claim: The US Dollar Index (DXY) has broken above 101, out of an almost 18-month range between 97 and 100, and is heading back toward 52-week highs. The euro, sterling and Canadian dollar are all losing major supports.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: A DXY move to 52-week highs together with rate stress would immediately disrupt risk assets.

insights.claim: Patrick Ceresna argues the dollar rally is not a rate-differential trade, since short-term rates are rising everywhere including Europe and Canada. He reads it as a possible sign of emerging dollar funding stress, which the bond market also shows.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: If the rally reflects funding stress rather than carry, it is a risk-off signal and not a benign rates story. Monitor cross-currency funding indicators.

insights.claim: The euro, the largest weight in the DXY, is the currency most vulnerable to breaking down. It is trading back at recent lows with possible downside to about 1.08-1.10 (quoted as '108 to 110').
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: Short EUR/USD is the cleanest expression of a continued dollar breakout, with a 1.08-1.10 target zone.

insights.claim: Crude oil's pullback from about $105 (after a run from about $80 in two weeks) is a headline-driven pause, not a real improvement in supply. It is a typical 50% retracement to the 50-day moving average, while global inventories are depleted and only demand destruction can fix them.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: Ceresna says a spike to $110-120/bbl is 'completely on the table'. A breakout from around $90 is the key trigger next week and would add to bond-market stress.
insights.quote: can we see 110 or $120 barrel of oil? I think it's completely on the table

insights.claim: Gold's early-August breakout came when the Treasury signaled intervention in the long end of the curve. It may be a false start: rising real yields and a stronger dollar since Jackson Hole never gave bulls confirmation, and gold sits just below its 50-day moving average but still inside its Fibonacci zones.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: If DXY makes new highs, yields keep rising and gold stays below its 50-day moving average, Ceresna would push the next gold bull leg out to late Q4 or Q1 next year.

insights.claim: Copper positioning is crowded long (100th-percentile bullish COT positioning). But after a tariff-driven 7% drop, dip buyers took it straight back to 52-week highs, so Patrick Ceresna respects the bull trend despite the crowding, with measured targets up to about 7.25 (quoted as '77 and a quarter').
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: Stay with copper longs while dips keep getting bought. Crowding alone is not a reason to fade it.

insights.claim: Spot uranium (U3O8) stays firm near 90 and the Sprott Physical Uranium Trust is stable, but uranium equities are fading rallies and attracting no flows. A break below 40 on URA, the global uranium ETF, would signal distribution with short-term downside to about $35.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: Uranium equities are underperforming physical uranium. Watch URA $40 support, and look for a base with no lower lows before buying for a possible Q4 accumulation cycle.

insights.claim: In two weeks, large speculators in Japanese yen futures swung from about 92,000 contracts net short to more than 120,000 net long, 100th-percentile long on a one-year lookback. Nearly 110,000 contracts flipped in a single week, more than the repositioning seen across all of 2022 or 2023.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna / co-host
insights.so_what: An extreme, fast positioning flip leaves the yen long crowd exposed to a squeeze.

insights.claim: The record yen-long positioning was built near the 65 handle on yen futures as of September 15. Since then the yen has dropped about 200 pips on the broad dollar rally, even after the Bank of Japan's rate hike, raising the risk that new yen bulls are caught and squeezed out.
insights.speaker: Patrick Ceresna
insights.so_what: The yen had turned technically bullish (above its 50-week moving average for the first time in over 1.5 years), but dollar funding stress threatens that thesis. Watch the next COT reports for long liquidation.
insights.quote: It's a crowding map that shows where traders are committed and where the price uh could make the crowd vulnerable.
